page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high-clock-speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES cryptography and bit manipulation via BMI2. The instance includes 16.0 GB of memory, equating to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates with 35 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1 data cache.

The system does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage, necessitating network-attached disks for root filesystems and persistent application data. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Without dedicated GPU hardware, graphical and massive matrix operations rely solely on host CPU vector units.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier execution across standardized synthetic workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1244.0 and a multi-core score of 4795.0, reflecting consistent single-thread responsiveness from its 3.1 GHz clock rate. Passmark testing reported an overall CPU score of 8939.31 and a memory score of 1981.81. Throughput measurements recorded 6.88 GB/sec in static web serving tests and 7.45 million operations per second during Redis SET operations. However, throughput constraints appear under heavy parallel compression, where bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scored in the lower quartile at 37.32 GB/sec. Similarly, local inference on a 7B language model remains limited to 6.44 tokens per second for generation and 11.39 tokens per second for prompt processing.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers an efficient resource balance for compute-bound services that do not require massive in-memory footprints, eliminating overhead costs associated with surplus memory allocations. Workloads matching this profile include Clang-based software compilation pipelines, API web servers, microservices, batch processing, and mid-tier caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance tailored for compute-heavy workloads. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor on the x86_64 architecture, the server features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions and 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for system operations, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without integrated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place the instance in the middle tier of general compute efficiency, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 4795.0 and Redis throughput of 7.45 million SET operations per second. Its lean memory footprint and sustained core frequencies make it appropriate for continuous integration pipelines, web serving clusters, and batch data processing.
